cohort: 498 pregnant women treated with papaverine at a large tertiary center between February 2010 and October 2019, and 498 randomly selected pregnancies resulting in live births from the same institution
finding: Short-term gestational exposure to papaverine, when adjusted for indication, was not associated with an increased risk of major malformations, preterm deliveries, cesarean sections, lower birth weight, small for gestational age, or perinatal death.
